name: Original creatures in Roblox-inspired world
description: Original creatures's character in the Roblox-inspired world world. World: A bright block-toy world: soft plastic bricks, stud-textured baseplate, tidy houses, fences, block trees and drifting block clouds, with a chunky block character whose painted face really acts. Character: Original small expressive characters, the 'Pips': a smooth sculpted bean body, a dark glass visor whose glowing face acts (squints, widens, droops, lip-syncs), an antenna bulb that reacts to mood, mitten hands, boots, optional headset.
rules: The visor face is the acting: eyes squint, widen, droop and look at things; the mouth follows the voice; the antenna bulb brightens on emphasis.
Each Pip has ONE body colour, the same cream belly and mitten hands, dark boots; a team is told apart by colour, antenna, headset and badge.
Smooth clay surfaces with a soft sheen: no hard edges on the characters, rounded props in the world.
Studs on the ground and a few props; flat saturated colour blocking; sun from the front-left with a soft shadow.
Environment tells the story: a tower grows, a storm darkens the sky, doors open. Props move; the character does not teleport.
Keep the camera low-key: moves only for reveals.
COMBINED STYLE: check scale (character height vs props) and colour contrast in the preview before approving.
camera_language: Small characters want a low, close camera at their eye level so they feel big and alive. Wide only to place them in the workshop; medium for talking (the visor face is the performance); medium-wide three-quarter to show what the hands are doing. Moves only on a reveal or a realisation, each with a reason. (Character framing from original-creatures; the world is roblox-inspired: keep shots inside its set.)
audio_direction: upbeat bed, boing on hops, pop on text
pitfalls: Over-the-shoulder shows only the round back: use medium-wide three-quarter.
At close-up the face crops: use medium-close-up for reactions.
The bright bulb on the antenna can bloom into the frame top: keep the camera lower than 1.1 m or bloom threshold above 0.85.
The wide torso blocks the object in over-the-shoulder: use medium-wide three-quarter.
references: reference videos ref1, ref4, ref7 (creature idea only)
